'''John David Brillhart''' (November 13, 1930 – May 21, 2022) was a mathematician who worked in [[number theory]] at the [[University of Arizona]].

==Early life and education==
Brillhart was born on November 13, 1930, in [[Berkeley, California]].<ref name="notices">{{cite journal |title=John Brillhart (1930–2022) |first1=Christian |last1=Ballot |first2=Richard |last2=Blecksmith |first3=Michael |last3=Filaseta |first4=Michael |last4=Morrison |first5=Patrick |last5=Morton |first6=Samuel S. |last6=Wagstaff Jr. |authorlink6=Samuel S. Wagstaff Jr. |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202209/rnoti-p1469.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=69 |issue=9 |date=October 2022 |page=1469}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n83124401.html|title = Brillhart, John, 1930- - LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies &#124; Library of Congress, from LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress)}}</ref>

He studied at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he received his A.B. in 1953, his M.A. in 1966, and his Ph.D. in 1967.<ref name="notices"/><ref name=phd>{{MathGenealogy|id=32104}}</ref> His doctoral thesis in mathematics was supervised by [[D. H. Lehmer]], with assistance from [[Leonard Carlitz]].<ref name="notices"/>

Before becoming a mathematician, he served in the [[United States Army]].<ref name="notices"/>

==Career==
Brillhart joined the faculty at the [[University of Arizona]] in 1967 and retired in 2001.<ref name="notices"/> He advised two Ph.D. students.<ref name="notices"/>

==Research==
Brillart worked in [[integer factorization]]. His joint work with Michael A. Morrison in 1975 describes how to implement the [[continued fraction factorization]] method originally developed by Lehmer and [[Ralph Ernest Powers]] in 1931.<ref name="notices"/><ref name="morrison-brillhart">{{cite journal |last=Morrison |first=Michael A. |author2=Brillhart, John |title=A Method of Factoring and the Factorization of ''F''<sub>7</sub> |journal=[[Mathematics of Computation]] |volume=29 |issue=129 |pages=183–205 |date=January 1975 |doi=10.2307/2005475 |jstor=2005475 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}<!--|accessdate=May 13, 2007 --></ref> One consequence was the first factorization of the [[Fermat number]] <math>F^7 = 2^{2^7}+1</math>.<ref name="notices"/><ref name="morrison-brillhart"/> Their ideas were influential in the development of the [[quadratic sieve]] by [[Carl Pomerance]].<ref name="notices"/>

Brillhart was a member of the [[Cunningham Project]], which factors [[Mersenne number|Mersenne]], Fermat, and related numbers.<ref name="notices"/> He was also a founding member and financial contributor to the [[Number Theory Foundation]] started by [[John L. Selfridge]].<ref name="notices"/>
